paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Following Jesus is not a plan for staying comfortable. He sends the twelve out with no money, no bag and no spare tunic, and He still says "the worker is worthy of his provisions" (Matthew 10:10). He tells them plainly that it will get hard, and He tells them just as plainly that they're not going out alone.

So what do you do when the road gets rough? Jesus says to be "as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves" (Matthew 10:16). Sharp eyes AND a clean heart, both at once. When they're handed over, He says "it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you" (Matthew 10:20). I rehearse speeches for my oven, so I LOVE that nobody has to have it all figured out ahead of time.

Then comes the part that keeps a baker steady. Jesus says "the one who perseveres to the end will be saved" (Matthew 10:22), and He reminds them that a disciple is not above his teacher (Matthew 10:24). If they get treated the way He was, they're in the very place He already stood. So when following Him costs you something, friend, don't be shocked and don't quit. Keep going, because the One who sent you knows the road.
